idiom_name: plain class or frozen object literal + explicit row<->value functions
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no declarative mapping layer, so the value is an ordinary class (or a frozen object literal) and the decompose/recompose pair is two small functions around the driver's row object. node:sqlite returns rows as plain objects keyed by column name, so the recompose half is a constructor call and the write half is one bound parameter per field; Object.freeze gives the immutability the pattern assumes, and structuredClone or spread gives the 'replace the whole value' semantics. The classic structure is therefore hand-written, but it is small: keep the column names in one place per value type instead of spelling them out in every query.
pitfalls: Object.freeze is shallow: a nested object or array inside the value can still be mutated behind other holders, so deep-freeze or store primitives only.
The row object's key names are the column names, so a renamed column breaks the recompose step silently at runtime - there is no compile-time check unless TypeScript types are applied.
SQLite drivers in JavaScript are synchronous (DatabaseSync) or driver-specific: sharing the value-mapping helpers across an async driver requires the mapping to stay pure and driver-agnostic.
